units: API list prices in USD per 1M tokens

none.label: Instant
none.desc: Answers right away with no extra reasoning. For lookups, rewrites and simple replies.

low.label: Low
low.desc: Quick responses with a little thinking. The least time and usage, for clear and simple asks.

medium.label: Medium
medium.desc: Balanced thinking. A solid starting point for most everyday work.

high.label: High
high.desc: Deeper reasoning for multi-step problems where a slip would matter.

xhigh.label: Extra high
xhigh.desc: Careful research and planning. For demanding, high-stakes work.

max.label: Max
max.desc: The strongest single-model effort. Slow and costly, so save it for the hardest problems.

ultra.label: Ultra
ultra.desc: Maximum effort plus subagents that work on parts of the job in parallel.

quick.label: Quick question
quick.desc: about 2K tokens in and 600 out at Medium

paper.label: Summarize a paper
paper.desc: a 10-page paper in, a structured summary out (15K in, 2K out at Medium)

data.label: Analyze a dataset
data.desc: a large file in, a full write-up out (60K in, 6K out at Medium)

claude.label: Claude
claude.h1: Which Claude model should you use?
claude.lede: Start with Opus 5.5 on Medium. Move up to Fable for the hardest work, and down to Sonnet or Haiku when the work is simple.
claude.naming: The names grow with the work: a haiku is three lines, a sonnet fourteen, an opus a major piece, a fable a whole story and a mythos a world.
claude.effortNote: Opus 5.5 defaults to Medium. Most other Claude models default to High. Every current model offers Low through Max.

models.name: Mythos 5.2
models.tagline: The most capable tier, held back from the public for now.
models.note: Mythos 5.2 shares its underlying model with Fable 5.2, without Fable’s extra safeguards for biology and cybersecurity. A small group of trusted organizations use it through Project Glasswing.

price.note: Same rates as Fable 5.2, invitation only

access.label: Defense Access
access.desc: Security operations, incident response, malware analysis and vulnerability triage. Organizations and individuals can apply.

access.label: Red Team Access
access.desc: Authorized penetration testing, red teaming and exploit development. Organizations only.

access.label: Specialized Access
access.desc: Authorized testing of critical infrastructure, with the fewest blocks. A limited set of verified organizations.

models.name: Fable 5.2
models.tagline: For your toughest challenges: open-ended technical and research work.
models.note: Fable thinks problems through before answering. Responses take longer and are the heaviest on your usage.
best: Open-ended research questions with no clear answer
Hard technical work in the sciences, finance and code
Jobs where a wrong answer is expensive
models.skip: Routine writing and quick questions. You pay more and wait longer for the same answer.
models.where: Claude apps and API. Released 9 Nov 2026.

models.name: Opus 5.5
models.tagline: Your daily driver for complex coding and knowledge work.
models.note: Opus uses more of your limit than Sonnet, but often finishes harder work in fewer turns. Its default effort is Medium.
best: Most real work: analysis, writing, planning and code
Tasks with several steps, files or sources
Any time you are unsure which model to pick
models.skip: Thousands of tiny repeat jobs. Haiku does those for a fraction of the cost.
models.where: Claude apps and API. Released 22 Sep 2026.

models.name: Sonnet 5.5
models.note: Sonnet answers faster and uses less of your limit than Opus, with some tradeoff in quality on harder work.
best: Clear tasks with a known shape: summaries, drafts, rewrites
Everyday coding from a clear spec
When Opus is breezing through your work
models.skip: Messy problems with hidden traps. Move up to Opus.

models.name: Haiku 5.5
models.tagline: The fastest and cheapest. A supporting player, not a daily driver.
models.note: Haiku is less effective on complex work. Its price rises five-fold for prompts over 100,000 tokens.
best: High-volume jobs: tagging, extracting, formatting
Quick lookups and short rewrites
Helper agents inside bigger workflows
models.skip: Anything that needs judgment, nuance or long reasoning.
models.where: Mainly the Claude API, for building apps and helpers.

openai.label: OpenAI
openai.h1: Which OpenAI model should you use?
openai.lede: Start with GPT-6.1 Sol on Medium. Move up to Astra when Sol falls short, and down to Luna for fast, high-volume work.
openai.naming: Each tier is a bigger body in the sky: the Moon, the Earth, the Sun and then the stars.
openai.effortNote: In ChatGPT’s Chat tab you pick Instant, Medium, High or Extra High (run by GPT-6 Sol), or Pro (run by Astra). ChatGPT Work and Codex add Max and Ultra. The API calls the levels none, low, medium, high, xhigh and max.

api.low: API: low · Light in ChatGPT Work
api.xhigh: API: xhigh · Extra High in ChatGPT

models.name: GPT-6 Astra
models.tagline: For the toughest, most creative, long-horizon tasks.
models.note: In ChatGPT’s Chat tab it appears as GPT-6 Pro (Pro, Business and Enterprise plans). Plus plans get Astra in ChatGPT Work and Codex. It always reasons, so there is no Instant setting.
best: Long projects that run for hours
The hardest research, math and science tasks
Work where a mistake is costly
models.skip: Everyday work. GPT-6.1 Sol gets close for a fifth of the price.
models.where: API, ChatGPT Work and Codex, and GPT-6 Pro in Chat. Released 3 Sep 2026.

models.name: GPT-6.1 Sol
models.tagline: Near-Astra intelligence for important everyday work, at a fifth of the price.
models.note: GPT-6.1 Sol runs in ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API. In the Chat tab, GPT-6 Sol powers Instant through Extra High.
best: Most daily work: writing, analysis and code
Multi-step tasks and agents on a budget
Your default when unsure
models.skip: The very hardest science problems. OpenAI still points those to Astra.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Terra
models.tagline: The balanced middle tier from the GPT-5.6 family.
models.note: GPT-6 has no Terra. GPT-6.1 Sol now costs less per output token, so Terra mainly matters for tools already built on it.
best: Workflows already tuned on GPT-5.6
Balanced cost and quality on routine work
models.skip: New projects. Start with GPT-6.1 Sol instead.
models.where: API and the ChatGPT Work model list.

models.name: GPT-6 Luna
models.tagline: The fastest and cheapest, built for high-volume work.
models.note: Luna is optimized for fast responses at volume. Sol has more reasoning capability.
best: Sorting, tagging and extracting at scale
Quick replies and simple rewrites
Helper agents under Sol or Astra
models.where: API, ChatGPT and Codex. Released 22 Sep 2026.

gemini.label: Gemini
gemini.h1: Which Gemini model should you use?
gemini.lede: Start with Gemini 4 Argon on Medium. Drop to 3.8 Flash for quick, high-volume work.
gemini.naming: Gemini 4 models are named after elements, and the names are not a ranking: Carbon (6) sits above Argon (18).
gemini.effortNote: Gemini has three thinking levels: Low, Medium (the default) and High. Need more depth than High? Move up a model.

models.name: Gemini 4 Carbon
models.tagline: Google’s most capable model, built on Gemini 4 Argon.
models.note: Announced 28 Oct 2026. For now only cyber defenders and trusted partners in Google’s Fairwind program can use it, and there is no public API.

price.note: Announced intro price; no public API yet

models.name: Gemini 4 Argon
models.tagline: Google’s flagship you can use today, for hard reasoning, science and long outputs.
models.note: Generally available since 13 Oct 2026, with a 1M-token context window. Its default thinking level is Medium.

price.note: Intro price until 30 Nov; $4 / $20 from 1 Dec

best: Complex analysis of long documents
Science and math reasoning
Very long outputs
models.skip: Simple high-volume jobs. 3.8 Flash is cheaper and faster.
models.where: Gemini API, AI Studio and the Gemini app for eligible Google AI subscribers.

models.name: Gemini 4 Hydrogen
models.tagline: A fast Gemini 4 Flash model, reported to be in internal testing.
models.note: Not released. Business Insider reported on 11 Nov 2026 that Google staff are testing it. No price or date yet.

models.name: Gemini 3.8 Flash
models.tagline: Google’s most intelligent Flash: a fast, low-cost workhorse.
models.note: In the Gemini app for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers, in AI Mode and in Sheets. For the very cheapest calls, Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite costs $0.30 / $2.50.

price.note: Intro price until 31 Dec; $1.50 / $7.50 from 1 Jan 2027

best: Everyday tasks at speed
Coding and agent loops at scale
Helpers inside spreadsheets and documents
models.skip: The hardest reasoning. Step up to Argon.
